```{r Pulling the Questions from WVS that go in the Authoritarian Values Index}

library(tidyverse)
file.exists("WVS_Time_Series_1981-2022_rds_v5_0.rds")


# These are the standardized "Integrated" codes for the Time Series file
target_vars <- c(
  "S002VS",    # Wave number
  "S003",    # Country Code (Numeric)
  "S020",    # Year
  "E114",    # Strong Leader (Equivalent to Q235 / V127)
  "E117",    # Army Rule (Equivalent to Q238 / V130)
  "E115",    # Having Experts Rule
  "E116",    # Expert Rule (Equivalent to Q237 / V129)
  "E018",    # Respect for Authority (Equivalent to Q45 / V69)
  "A042",    # Obedience (Equivalent to Q17 / V21)
  "E232",    # Religious Law (Equivalent to Q252 / V155)
  "E233",    # Army Takeover (Equivalent to Q253 / V156)
  "A124_02", # Neighbor: Race
  "A124_06", # Neighbor: Immigrants
  "A124_09", # Neighbor: Religion
  "A124_12"  # Neighbor: Language
)

# Read just the column names to see what we are dealing with
names(read_rds("WVS_Time_Series_1981-2022_rds_v5_0.rds")) %>% head(20)


# Load the file using the corrected path and selection
# Ensure the filename matches exactly what is in your folder
wvs_subset <- read_rds("WVS_Time_Series_1981-2022_rds_v5_0.rds") %>%
  select(all_of(target_vars))

# Check that it loaded correctly
head(wvs_subset)

```

```{r Creating the Authoritarian_values_index}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven) # For zap_labels

wvs_indexed <- wvs_subset %>%
  # --- STEP 1: STRIP LABELS ---
  # This converts all 'haven_labelled' columns into standard numbers
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(zap_labels(.)))) %>%
  
  # --- STEP 2: PERFORM RECODING ---
  mutate(
    # Political Systems (1=Very Good, 4=Very Bad)
    auth_leader  = (5 - E114) / 3, 
    auth_army    = (5 - E117) / 3,
    auth_experts = (5 - E116) / 3,
    
    # Values (Respect for Authority E018: 1=Good, 3=Bad)
    auth_respect = (4 - E018) / 2,
    
    # Obedience (A042: 1=Mentioned, 2=Not Mentioned)
    auth_obey    = ifelse(A042 == 1, 1, 0),
    
    # Democracy Definitions (1=Not Essential, 10=Essential)
    auth_relig_law = (E232 - 1) / 9,
    auth_army_take = (E233 - 1) / 9,
    
    # Neighbors (1=Mentioned/Reject, 2=Not Mentioned)
    reject_race  = ifelse(A124_02 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_immig = ifelse(A124_06 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_relig = ifelse(A124_09 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_lang  = ifelse(A124_12 == 1, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  # --- STEP 3: CREATE THE INDEX ---
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(authoritarian_values_index = mean(c(
    auth_leader, auth_army, auth_experts, auth_respect, auth_obey,
    auth_relig_law, auth_army_take, reject_race, reject_immig, 
    reject_relig, reject_lang
  ), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()



# 1. Get a statistical summary of the new index
# This will show you the Min, Max, Mean, and how many NAs (missing values) exist
summary(wvs_indexed$authoritarian_values_index)

# 2. Visualize the distribution
# A successful index should usually look like a "bell curve" or be slightly skewed,
# ranging from 0 to 1.
hist(wvs_indexed$authoritarian_values_index, 
     main = "Distribution of Authoritarian Values Index",
     xlab = "Index Score (0 = Low, 1 = High)", 
     col = "steelblue", 
     breaks = 50)

# 3. Check the first few rows of just the components and the final index
wvs_indexed %>%
  select(S003, S020, auth_leader, auth_army, auth_experts, authoritarian_values_index) %>%
  head(10)
```


```{r Checking List of Countries in the Authoritarian_values_index}
# Install the missing package
install.packages("countrycode")

library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(countrycode)

# Recode and Create Index
wvs_indexed <- wvs_subset %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(zap_labels(.)))) %>%
  mutate(
    auth_leader    = (5 - E114) / 3, 
    auth_army      = (5 - E117) / 3,
    auth_experts   = (5 - E116) / 3,
    auth_respect   = (4 - E018) / 2,
    auth_obey      = ifelse(A042 == 1, 1, 0),
    auth_relig_law = (E232 - 1) / 9,
    auth_army_take = (E233 - 1) / 9,
    reject_race    = ifelse(A124_02 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_immig   = ifelse(A124_06 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_relig   = ifelse(A124_09 == 1, 1, 0),
    reject_lang    = ifelse(A124_12 == 1, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(authoritarian_values_index = mean(c(
    auth_leader, auth_army, auth_experts, auth_respect, auth_obey,
    auth_relig_law, auth_army_take, reject_race, reject_immig, 
    reject_relig, reject_lang
  ), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()


# Generate the list of countries
country_list <- wvs_indexed %>%
  filter(!is.na(authoritarian_values_index)) %>%
  distinct(S003) %>%
  mutate(country_name = countrycode(S003, origin = "iso3n", destination = "country.name")) %>%
  arrange(country_name)

# Display the list
print(country_list, n = Inf)

```


```{r Fixed Merging Script}
library(vdemdata)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Surgical extraction of the 6 core variables
vdem_indicators <- vdemdata::vdem %>%
  filter(year >= 1980) %>%
  select(
    country_text_id, 
    year, 
    v2x_polyarchy, 
    polarization = v2cacamps,
    party_strength = v2xps_party,
    digital_proxy = v2mecenefm
  )

# 2. Memory Cleanup: Delete the massive master object to free up RAM for the merge
rm(vdem)
gc() 

# 3. Final verification
names(vdem_indicators)

  
```




```{r Download and Load SWIID Directly}
library(tidyverse)
library(countrycode)

# Link for the latest SWIID v9.91
swiid_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fsolt/swiid/master/data/swiid_summary.csv"

# Load the data
swiid_raw <- read_csv(swiid_url)

# Clean using the updated 'gini_disp' column name
swiid_clean <- swiid_raw %>%
  select(country, year, gini_disp) %>% # 'gini_disp' replaces 'gini_net'
  mutate(iso3c = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "iso3c")) %>%
  select(-country)

# Success Check
head(swiid_clean)

```

```{r Triple Merge Script}
library(tidyverse)
library(WDI)
library(countrycode)
library(zoo)

# --- 1. PREPARE V-DEM (Political/Institutional) ---
# We use the specific names we discovered: v2xps_party and v2mecenefm
vdem_clean <- vdem_indicators %>%
  select(country_text_id, year, v2x_polyarchy, 
         polarization, party_strength, digital_proxy)

# --- 2. PREPARE WORLD BANK (Wealth/Resources) ---
# Ensuring no duplicates to avoid the many-to-many warning
wb_clean <- wb_data_clean %>%
  distinct(iso3c, year, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(iso3c, year, resource_rents, gni_pc)

# --- 3. PREPARE SWIID (Inequality) ---
# Using 'gini_disp' which we confirmed is the correct 2026 column name
swiid_clean_final <- swiid_clean %>%
  distinct(iso3c, year, .keep_all = TRUE)

# --- 4. PREPARE WVS (Authoritarian Values) ---
# Fixing the Northern Ireland (909) code and removing duplicates
wvs_final_clean <- wvs_indexed %>%
  mutate(iso3c = countrycode(S003, origin = "iso3n", destination = "iso3c",
                            custom_match = c("909" = "GBR"))) %>%
  distinct(iso3c, S020, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(iso3c, year = S020, authoritarian_values_index)

# --- 5. THE MASTER MERGE ---
final_regression_df <- vdem_clean %>%
  inner_join(wb_clean, by = c("country_text_id" = "iso3c", "year")) %>%
  inner_join(swiid_clean_final, by = c("country_text_id" = "iso3c", "year")) %>%
  inner_join(wvs_final_clean, by = c("country_text_id" = "iso3c", "year")) %>%
  # Create logged wealth and handle minor NAs
  mutate(logged_wealth = log(gni_pc)) %>%
  group_by(country_text_id) %>%
  mutate(resource_filled = na.approx(resource_rents, na.rm = FALSE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Keep only the rows where we have all 7 predictors
  drop_na(v2x_polyarchy, polarization, resource_filled, logged_wealth, 
          gini_disp, digital_proxy, party_strength, authoritarian_values_index)

# --- 6. SUCCESS CHECK ---
cat("Total Observations for Analysis:", nrow(final_regression_df), "\n")
head(final_regression_df)



```

```{r Regression Model}
# THE 7-WAY REGRESSION
final_model <- lm(scale(v2x_polyarchy) ~ 
                    scale(polarization) + 
                    scale(resource_filled) + 
                    scale(logged_wealth) + 
                    scale(gini_disp) + 
                    scale(digital_proxy) + 
                    scale(party_strength) + 
                    scale(authoritarian_values_index), 
                  data = final_regression_df)

summary(final_model)


```

```{r Coefficient Plot}
# 1. Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 2. Convert the model results into a "tidy" format for plotting
# This calculates the 95% Confidence Intervals automatically
plot_data <- tidy(final_model, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean up the names for the chart labels
    Variable = case_when(
      term == "scale(polarization)" ~ "Social Polarization",
      term == "scale(resource_filled)" ~ "Resource Rents",
      term == "scale(logged_wealth)" ~ "Wealth (Logged GDP)",
      term == "scale(gini_disp)" ~ "Inequality (Gini)",
      term == "scale(digital_proxy)" ~ "Digital Control/Censorship",
      term == "scale(party_strength)" ~ "Political Party Strength",
      term == "scale(authoritarian_values_index)" ~ "Public Auth. Values",
      TRUE ~ term
    )
  )

# 3. Create the Visualization
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(Variable, estimate), y = estimate)) +
  # Draw the error bars (Confidence Intervals)
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), 
                  color = "#2c3e50", size = 0.8) +
  # Highlight significant variables in a different color
  geom_point(data = filter(plot_data, p.value < 0.05), 
             color = "#e74c3c", size = 3) +
  # Add the vertical 'Zero' line
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  # Flip the coordinates for easier reading
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Which Factors Drive Authoritarianism?",
    subtitle = "                         Standardized Coefficients",
    x = "",
    y = "Impact on Democracy Score",
    caption = "Source: V-Dem, World Bank, SWIID, and World Values Survey"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )


```
